root_cause: The semantic writer owns a required raw depends_on array while the Typed Goal Graph compiler does not derive executable semantic edges from typed result consumption. Runtime and executable test fixtures therefore preserve multiple dependency representations without a single deterministic writer.
causal_chain: DECLARE_TURN_GOALS_SCHEMA requires the model to emit depends_on and offers no current_goal_output input binding.
Frozen semantics preserve the raw claim while typed graph compilation cannot trace that claim to a typed input source.
Pre-tool, workflow and scripted smoke fixtures consume or assert legacy dependency arrays, so a cutover limited to production modules leaves executable alternate writers.
Probabilistic declarations and legacy fixture oracles can therefore add or omit edges independently of the deterministic graph.
rejected_hypotheses: This is not a phrase-specific pronoun defect because the raw dependency writer is structural for every provider declaration.
Another model verifier cannot establish deterministic execution authority because it would remain a second probabilistic graph writer.
Production-only cutover is insufficient because executable semantic fixtures still submit and compare the retired raw edge contract.
affected_boundaries: executable semantic fixture and smoke validation
